title: Decision JM-6: hub errors map to serverUnavailable or invalidArguments
description: The draft defines only serverUnavailable ('if the hub cannot be reached'). Chosen: transport errors and hub 5xx -> serverUnavailable; hub 4xx -> invalidArguments with a description.
notes:
Amended 2026-10-18 (Mark, audit item 9): transport errors, 5xx and 429 (PeerError::Rejected, peer.rs:422) -> serverUnavailable; other 4xx -> invalidArguments with description; RelayError::InvalidResponse -> serverFail; RelayError::Hub(HubError) from the local hub (no HTTP status) uses respond()'s classes at http.rs:262-289: InvalidRequest -> invalidArguments, everything else -> serverFail.
CORRECTION 2026-10-18 (Mark): supersedes the local-HubError clause above. A local HubError is first mapped to the HTTP status respond() gives it (http.rs:262-289: NoSuchRoom 404, InvalidRequest 400, UnverifiedAbusiveMessage 422, NotImplemented 501, Peer/InvalidPeerResponse 502, other 500), then the same status rule as a remote hub applies (429/5xx -> serverUnavailable, other 4xx -> invalidArguments). One rule for local and remote hubs.
